The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater Levels :  In  August  2025,  In  Post-monsoon 2025, around 90% of the country's monitoring stations exhibited a depth to water level within 10 meters below ground level. Deeper  water  levels  of  more  than  20  m  are  observed  in  around  5%  of  stations  of  the country  covering  mainly  the  western  states,  especially  Western  Rajasthan,  Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
2.  The deeper groundwater level in the states like Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh  during  Post-monsoon  2025  has  been  significantly  influenced  by  the  over extraction of groundwater compared to the recharge during the monsoon period.
3.  Annual  water  level  comparison  with  the  previous  year  Post-monsoon  2024  to  Postmonsoon  2025  has  shown  that  about  63%  of  total  analyzed  stations  of  the  country experienced rise in  annual  water level fluctuation may  be  attributed to the less groundwater extraction compared to 2024.
4.  About 73% of the analyzed stations of the unconfined aquifer experienced a rise of water level  in  the  decadal  mean  water  level  fluctuation  of  2015-2024  with  respect  to  Postmonsoon 2025.
5.  The  Groundwater  Drought  Indices  indicate  that  in Post-monsoon  2025 ,  groundwater conditions  across  India  remained  largely  stable,  with 91%  of  monitoring  stations showing no  deficit .  However,  localized  deficits  were  observed  in  several  regions  notably in Meghalaya, Nagaland, and the Dadar Nagar Havili & Daman & Diu.
- c) Fertilizers : The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
4. Pests & Diseases : Intensity of pests and diseases at some fields has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Citrus (Gummosis) and Chilli (Leaf curl) in Maharashtra. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being
carried  out.  The  overall  intensity  of  pests  and  diseases  remained  below  the  Economic Threshold Level.

data.heading: Week 1 (27 Feb - 05 March 2026):
data.text: -  Maximum  temperatures  are  likely  to  be  above  normal  by  3-5°C  over  many  parts  of Northwest India during the week.

data.heading: Details of each Segment
data.text:
-  Positive departures of maximum temperatures are likely to spread towards West, Central, East and northern Peninsular India and they are likely to be above normal by 2-4°C over these regions towards the end of the week.
-  Minimum  temperature  is  likely  to  be  above  normal  in  many  parts  of  NW  India,  Bihar, Gujarat  state,  some  parts  of  Madhya  Maharashtra,  many  parts  of  M.P.,  South  Karnataka, some  parts  of  Tamil  Nadu,  Rayalseema,  Southern  parts  of  CAP  and  NE  India.  TMIN  is likely  to  be  below  normal  in  many  parts  of  East  India,  many  parts  of  Maharashtra  and Kerala.

data.heading: Week 2 (06 March - 12 March 2026):
data.text:
-  Maximum temperatures  are  likely  to  be  above  normal  (by  3-5°C)  over  most  parts  of  the country except central & adjoining peninsular India, where they are likely to be near normal or slightly below normal by 1-2°C.
-  Minimum  temperatures  are  likely  to  be  above  normal  (by  1-3°C)  over  most  parts  of northwest and northeast India, and below normal (by 2-4°C) over most parts of east, central, and peninsular India.

data.heading: Rabi Crops - Area coverage
data.text:
-  Rice: About 21.80 lakh ha area coverage under Summer Rice has been reported as compared to 23.45 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
-  Pulses: About 1.15 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 1.03 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
-  Oilseeds: About  1.69  lakh  ha  area  coverage  has  been  reported  compared  to  1.26  lakh  ha during the corresponding period of last year.
